_info: Model registry for the fence detector (YOLO11n, 7 classes). One entry per released model (the drone's in models, the ground robot's in ground_models): where it is used, the data and code it came from, how it was trained, how it scored offline and live, and the sha256 of every file. Weights are attached to the GitHub release named in 'release'; TensorRT engines are built on the Jetson (hardware-specific) and live in ~/querra-scout-20261107/models/fence-yolo. 'python3 tools/model_registry.py' validates this file and rebuilds the table in ml/README.md; '--check DIR' compares local files with the hashes. 'summary' is the one-line change shown on the charts; 'platform' says from which platform release the model is the default (default_from) or runs the live simulation (live_sim_from).

statuses.default: the model the system uses unless told otherwise (ROS 2 detector, replay demo, field mode)
statuses.live-sim: used for live Gazebo flights (ros.sh demo tcp://...), not the default elsewhere
statuses.retired: kept for comparison; not used by default
statuses.candidate: better than the default offline; waits for live tests before it is used by default
statuses.not adopted: trained and scored, not better than the default where it counts; kept for comparison, never used by default

models.decision: Not adopted: model-v0.5's mix plus only the 1,500 steel-wire and polywire frames (no wire boxes), trained exactly like the control model-v0.8, so those frames are the only difference. They are the cause of model-v0.6's and model-v0.7's false broken wires: against the control, false-break frames from 0.7 rose on 3 of the 4 test stream sets (0.1-0.5% to 0.4-1.6%) and in the mission replay (1 to 5; from 0.5, 4 to 23), and break boxes came back at model-v0.7's corner (6 frames from 0.5, the control none). They also made it more sure of true breaks, so at the same false-break rate it matches or beats model-v0.5 on 5 of the 6 stream sets but finds fewer on the classic flight test farms (15% against 23% at 0.4% false). And they cost wires on rope and tape (wire mAP50 0.881 and 0.747, model-v0.5 0.952 and 0.966). The gain is the best yet on fallen posts on thin wire (81% and 82% from 0.7, model-v0.5 59% and 61%), and its wire_break mAP50 is higher than model-v0.5's on 8 of the 9 held-out sets. The mission replay is clean at the drone's settings (3 of 3, 0 false), but with 5 times the false-break frames of model-v0.5 and no flight, model-v0.5 stays the default.

models.decision: Not adopted: a control run, model-v0.5 fine-tuned 8 more epochs on its own mix with nothing added, the settings of model-v0.6 and model-v0.7. It answers its question: the extra training did not raise false broken wires (wb_false 0.0-0.5% on the stream sets, model-v0.5 0.0-1.2%; 1 false frame from 0.7 in the replay, 0 false alerts), so the data model-v0.6 and model-v0.7 added did, first suspect the steel-wire and polywire frames both share. But it is not better: less sure of every break, it finds fewer on the flight test farms (9% from 0.7, model-v0.5 23% and 16%), is lower on every held-out set (wire_break mAP50 -0.003 to -0.034), and on TTPLA's real photos boxes false branches in 19.5% from 0.5 (model-v0.5 1.0%) and false cows in 36% from 0.7 (25%): repeating the same data overfits.

The false alert is the corner post 57 m from F1, as model-v0.6's: 6 frames with a break box there from 0.7 (model-v0.5: 1, model-v0.6: 5). With wire_break counted from 0.75: 3 alerts, 0 false, a threshold chosen on model-v0.6's replay

models.decision: Not adopted: model-v0.5 stays the default. The corner negatives did not lower false broken wires: frames with a false break from conf 0.7 doubled on the four test stream sets (0.8-2.3%, model-v0.5 0.3-1.2%), 8 false frames in the mission replay (1), and the same false alert at the corner as model-v0.6. From 0.75 or 0.8 it does not beat model-v0.5 on both breaks found and false frames on the flight test farms (wb_thresholds.json). Gained fallen posts on thin wire from 0.7 (steel 70%, polywire 72%; v0.5 59%, 61%), higher val mAP50 on the same set (0.957, 0.952), TTPLA close to v0.5. Lost wires on polytape (wire mAP50 0.778, v0.5 0.966) and polyrope (0.898, 0.952): thin wire without wire boxes needs the thick conductors beside it. Next: a control run (model-v0.5 fine-tuned on its own mix) to tell whether the extra training or the thin-wire frames raise false breaks.

models.decision: Not adopted: model-v0.5 stays the default. Better on real conductors where they show: fallen posts from conf 0.7 on steel wire 75% (v0.5: 59%), polywire 76% (61%), polyrope 85% (78%), polytape 91% (87%), and equal or higher mAP50 on every stream set and most held-out sets. But broken wires on real conductors are still not found (rope 3%, tape 8%, steel wire and polywire 0%), and it raises more false broken wires: 15 false frames from 0.7 in the mission replay (v0.5: 1) and one false confirmed alert (0), wb_false 0.2-1.2% on the four flight stream sets (0.0-0.4%), 3.5% of TTPLA's real photos with a false broken wire from 0.5 (0.4%). No threshold makes it as good as v0.5 on both broken-wire recall and false frames across the stream sets (wb_thresholds.json). The data that helped fallen posts can go into a later model with more negative examples.

ground_models.decision: Candidate. Better than ground-v0.1 offline on every check the alerts use: test mAP50 0.979 (0.957), fallen posts kept at conf 0.7 on the test forests 82% (52%), and on the four patrols every fault found with every class at 0.7, 29 of 29 (25 of 29), 0 false alerts. Not the default until it passes live patrols on the Jetson (its engine is not built yet). Keep class_conf fallen_post=0.5 until a live test at 0.7: offline, fallen posts show in 6-7 frames at 0.7 where 5 are needed, and ground-v0.1's live patrols showed 1-2 fewer than offline.

ground_models.decision: Candidate. On real fence conductors far better than ground-v0.2: on thin wire, wire mAP50 0.95 (steel 0.44, polywire 0.20) and broken wires found from conf 0.7 in 72-77% of the frames (17%, 1%). Nothing lost on the checks the alerts use: classic test mAP50 0.981 (0.979), and 29 of 29 faults with no false alert on the four patrols with every class at 0.7, with fallen posts from 0.5, and with broken wires from 0.6. Less confident on broken wires: on the classic test 79% from 0.7 (85%), 90% from 0.6, so with ground-v0.3 count broken wires from 0.6 (class_conf wire_break=0.6, fallen_post=0.5). Not the default until it passes live patrols on the Jetson (its engine is not built yet) and is checked on real footage: the thin wire is the simulator's 3x supersampled render.
